Ἀμιναδάβ.long: Amminadab, son of Ram and father of Nahshon, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Ἀμιναδάβ.as:
Ἀμιναδάβ, ὁ indecl. (Heb עַמִּינָדָב),
Amminadab: Mt 1:4, Lk 3:33 (WH om.).†

Ἀμώς.long: Amos, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, an ancestor of Jesus.
Ἀμώς.as:
Ἀμώς, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָמוֹץ, Is 1:1; עָמוֹס, Am 1:1; אָמוֹן, IV Ki 21:18 ff. B);
1. as in IV Ki 21:18 ff. B (Α. Ἀμμών; Jos., Ἀμμών, Ἄμωσσς), Amon: Mt 1:10.
2.Amos: Lk 3:25.†

ἁμαρτία.long: prop: missing the mark; hence: (a) guilt, sin, (b) a fault, failure (in an ethical sense), sinful deed.
ἁμαρτία.as:
ἁμαρτία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἁμαρτάνω, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for חַטָּאת and cogn. forms, also for פֶּשַׁע ,עָוֹן, etc.;]
prop. a missing the mark; in cl. (v. reff. to CR in MM, VGT, s.v.);
(a)guilt, sin (Plat., Arist., al.);
(b) more freq., from Æsch. down, a fault, failure. In NT (as LXX) always in ethical sense;
1. as a principle and quality of action, = τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν, a sinning, sin: Ro 5:12, 1320; ὑφ’ ἁμαρτίαν εἶναι, Ro 3:9; ἐπιμένειν, Ro 6:1; ἀποθνήσκειν, νεκρὸν εἶναι τῇ ἁ., Ro 6:2, 11; τὴν ἀ. γινώσκειν, Ro 7:7; σῶμα τῆς ἁ., Ro 6:6; ἀπάτη τῆς ἁ., He 3:13; personified as a ruling principle, ἁ. βασιλεύει, κυριεύει, etc., Ro 5:216:12, 147:17, 20; δουλεύειν, Ro 6:6; δοῦλος τῆς ἁ., ib. 17; νόμος τῆς ἁ., Ro 7:238:2; δύναμις τῆς ἁ., I Co 15:56 (cf. Ge 4:7).
2. As a generic term (disting. fr. the specific terms ἁμάρτημα, q.v., etc.) for concrete wrongdoing, violation of the divine law, sin: Jo 8:46, Ja 1:15, al.; ποιεῖν (τὴν) ἁ., Jo 8:34, II Co 11:7, I Jo 3:8; εἴχειν ἁ., Jo 9:4115:22, 2419:11, I Jo 1:8; in pl. ἁμαρτίαι, sin in the aggregate, I Th 2:16 (v. Milligan, in l.); ποιεῖν ἁμαρτίας, Ja 5:15; πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν, Ja 5:20, I Pe 4:8; ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν, Mt 26:28, Mk 1:4, al.; ἐν ἁμαρτίαις εἶναι, I Co 15:17; collectively, αἴρειν τὴν ἁ. τ. κόσμου, Jo 1:29; ἀποθνήσκειν ἐν τῇ ἁ., Jo 8:21.
3. = ἁμάρτημα, a sinful deed, a sin: Mt 12:31, Ac 7:60, I Jo 5:16.
SYN.: v.s. ἁμάρτημα.

ἀμφίβληστρον.long: prop: something thrown around; a fishing-net, drag-net.
ἀμφίβληστρον.sd: a (fishing) net (as thrown about the fish)
ἀμφίβληστρον.der: from a compound of the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G906 (βάλλω);
ἀμφίβληστρον.as:
ἀμφίβληστρον, -ου, τό
(< ἀμφιβάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם;]
something thrown around, as a garment; spec., a casting-net: Mt 4:18.†

ἀμήν.g: verily, truly, amen, so let it be
ἀμήν.long: verily, truly, amen; at the end of sentences may be paraphrased by: So let it be.
ἀμήν.sd: properly, firm, i.e. (figuratively) trustworthy; adverbially, surely (often as interjection, so be it)
ἀμήν.as:
ἀμήν, indecl. (Heb. אָמֵן, verbal adj. fr. אמן, to prop, ni., be firm),
[in LXX: I Ch 16:36, I Es 9:46, Ne 5:138:6, To 8:814:15, III Mac 7:23, IV Mac 18:24 (elsewhere א״ is rendered ἀληθινός, Is 65:16; ἀληθῶς, Je 35 (28):6; γένοιτο, Nu 5:22, De 27:15ff., III Ki 1:36, Ps 40 (41):1371 (72):19105 (106):48, Je 11:5)*.]
1. As adj. (cf. Is 65:16), ὁ ἀ., Re 3:14.
2. As adv.,
(a) in solemn assent to the statements or prayers of another (Nu 5:22, Ne 5:138:6 etc.): ὁ ἀ., I Co 14:16;
(b) similarly, at the end of one's own prayer or ascription of praise: Ro 1:2515:33, Ga 1:5, I Ti 1:17;
(c) in the Gospels, exclusively, introducing solemn statements of our Lord, truly, verily: Mt 5:18, 26Mk 3:28 (v. Swete, in l.), Lk 4:24, al.; ἀ. ἀ., always in Jo 1:523:35:19, al.; τὸ ναί, καὶ . . . τὸ ἀ., II Co 1:20 (on usage in π., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).

ἀμφιέννυμι.der: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and (to invest);
ἀμφιέννυμι.as:
ἀμφιέννυμι
(< ἕννυμι, to clothe),
to clothe: Mt 6:3011:8, Lk 7:25 (cf. ἀμφιάζω).†

ἄμμος.as:
ἄμμος, -ου, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for חוֹל;]
sand, sandy ground: Mt 7:26, Ro 9:27, He 11:12, Re 18:1, Re 20:8.†

ἁμαρτωλός.as:
ἁμαρτωλός, -όν
(< ἁμαρτάνω), [in LXX chiefly for רשׁﬠ;]
sinful, a sinner: of all men, I Ti 1:15; of those especially wicked, I Ti 1:9, I Pe 4:18; p1., Mt 9:10-1311:1926:45, al. (v. MM, VGT, s.v.; Cremer, 102, 634)

ἀμφότεροι.as:
ἀμφότεροι, -αι, -α
(replaces ἄμφω in κοινή, v. M, Pr., 57; used of more than two, Pr., 80; MM, VGT, s.v.),
both of two: Mt 9:17, al.

ἅμα.g: at the same time, along with
ἅμα.long: at the same time, therewith, along with, together with.
ἅμα.sd: properly, at the "same" time, but freely used as a preposition or adverb denoting close association
ἅμα.as:
ἅμα
adv.,
at once (Lat. simul): Ac 24:2627:40, Ro 3:12 (one and all = יַחַד, Ps 14:3), Col 4:3, I Ti 5:13, Phm 22; seq. σύν, I Th 4:175:10; as prep. c. dat., together with: Mt 13:29 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.); also, c. adv., ἅ. πρωΐ (cl., ἅ. ἕω, etc.), early in the morning: Mt 20:1.†

ἁμαρτάνω.long: originally: I miss the mark, hence (a) I make a mistake, (b) I sin, commit a sin (against God); sometimes the idea of sinning against a fellow-creature is present.
ἁμαρτάνω.sd: properly, to miss the mark (and so not share in the prize), i.e. (figuratively) to err, especially (morally) to sin
ἁμαρτάνω.kj: for your faults, offend, sin, trespass
ἁμαρτάνω.der: perhaps from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G3313 (μέρος);
ἁμαρτάνω.as:
ἁμαρτάνω
(pres. formed from aor. ἁμαρτεῖν), [in LXX for חטא, also for אשׁם, רשׁע, etc.;]
1.to miss the mark (Hom., Æsch., al.), hence metaph. (Hom., al.), to err, do wrong.
2. In LXX and NT, to violate God's law, to sin (for non-Christian exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.): absol., Mt 18:2527:4, Lk 17:3, Jo 5:148:119:2, 3, Ro 2:123:235:12, 14,166:15, I Co 7:28,3615:34, Eph 4:26, I Ti 5:20, Tit 3:11, He 3:1710:26, I Pe 2:20, II Pe 2:42:4I Jo 1:102:13:6,895:18; c. cogn. acc., ἁ. ἁμαρτίαν (cf. Ex 32:30, חֲטָאָהחָטָא), I Jo 5:16; seq. εἰς, Mt 18:21, Lk 15:18, 2117:4, Ac 25:8 (καίσαρα). I Co 6:188:12 (Field, Notes, 173); ἐνώπιον, Lk 15:18, 21; πρὸς θάνατον (cf. Nu 18:22, חֵטְא לָמוּת), I Jo 5:16 (Cremer, 98, 633).†

ἀμπελών.as:
ἀμπελών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(< ἄμπελος), [in LXX for כֶּרֶם;]
a vineyard: Mt 20:1 ff. Mt 21:28 ff, Lk 13:620:9 ff., I Co 9:7. Æschin., 49, 13; Diod., al.; v. MM, VGT, s.v.; LS, s.v. ἀμπελουργεῖον.)

ἀμελέω.long: I neglect, am careless of, disregard.
ἀμελέω.kj: make light of, neglect, be negligent, no regard
ἀμελέω.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3199 (μέλω);
ἀμελέω.as:
ἀμελέω, -ῶ
(< μέλει), [in LXX: Je 4:17 (מרה) Je 31:32 (בּעל), Wi 3:10, II Mac 4:14*;]
(a) absol., to be careless, not to care: Mt 22:5;
(b) c. gen., to be careless of, to neglect: I Ti 4:14, He 2:38:9 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἄμπελος.sd: a vine (as coiling about a support)
ἄμπελος.der: probably from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and that of G257 (ἅλων);
ἄμπελος.as:
ἄμπελος, -ου, ἡ,
[in LXX for גֶּפֶן;]
vine: Mt 26:29, Mk 14:25, Lk 22:18Ja 3:12; fig., of Christ, Jo 15:1, 4-5; of his enemies (on the usage here, v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Re 14:18, 19.†

ἀμέριμνος.long: free from anxiety (though anxiety is rather too strong a word) or care.
ἀμέριμνος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3308 (μέριμνα);
ἀμέριμνος.as:
** ἀμέριμνος, -ον
(< μέριμνα), [in LXX: Wi 6:157:23*;]
free from anxiety or care: Mt 28:14, I Co 7:32 (for exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀμφιβάλλω.as:
ἀμφι-βάλλω (v. supr.),
[in LXX: Hb 1:17*;]
= περιβάλλω, to throw around, as a garment: absol. (MM, VGT, s.v.), of casting a net: Mk 1:16 (Rec. βάλλονταν ἀμφίβληστρον).†

ἁμάρτημα.as:
ἁμάρτημα, -τος, τό
(< ἁμαρτεῖν, v. supr.), [in LXX for חַטָּאָה, עָוֺן etc.;]
an act of disobedience to divine law (Lft., Notes, 273), a sinful deed, a sin: Mk 3:28, 29, Ro 3:25, I Co 6:18, II Pe 1:9, WH, mg.; αἰώνιων ἁ. (DCG, i, 788a), Mk 3:29 (for exx. from π., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†
SYN.: ἀγνόημα, ἁμαρτία, ἀνομία, ἀσέβεια, ἥττημα, παράβασις, παρακοή, παρανομία, παράπτωμα (v. Cremer, 100; Tr., Syn., § lxvi; DB, iv, 532; DCG, i, 788a; Westc, Eph., 165 f.)

ἄμφοδον.long: prop: a road around anything; the street of a village.
ἄμφοδον.der: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G3598 (ὁδός);
ἄμφοδον.as:
ἄμφοδον, -ου, το
(< ἀμφί, ὁδός), [in LXX for אַרְמְנוֹן (Je 17:2730:1049:27)*;]
prop., a road around anything (RV, the open street): Mk 11:4, Ac 19:28, WH, mg.†

ἄμεμπτος.long: blameless, free from fault or defect.
ἄμεμπτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3201 (μέμφομαι);
ἄμεμπτος.as:
ἄ-μεμπτος, -ον
(< μέμφομσι), [in LXX chiefly for תָּם;]
blameless, free from fault (in π. of a marriage-contract; M, Th., I, 3:13; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.): Lk 1:6, Phl 2:153:6, I Th 3:13 (WH, mg., -ως) He 8:7.†
SYN.: ἄμωμος, ἀνέγκλητος, ἀνεπίλημπτος, q.v. (Tr., Syn., § ciii).

ἀμφιάζω.as:
ἀμφιάζω
(< ἀμφί, on both sides: v. M, Pr., 100), Hellenistic for ἀμφιέννυμι (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), [in LXX for לָבַשׁ, etc.;]
to clothe: Lk 12:28 (T, -έζει).†

ἀμπελουργός.as:
ἀμπελουργός, -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX for כֹּרֵם;]
a vine dresser: Lk 13:7.†

ἀμνός.long: a lamb (as a type of innocence, and with sacrificial connotation).
ἀμνός.as:
ἀμνός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for כֶּבֶשׂ;]
a lamb: fig., of Christ (DCG, ii, 620b), Jo 1:29, 36, Ac 8:32(LXX), I Pe 1:19 (cf. ἀρνίον; Cremer, 102, 635).†

ἀμύνομαι.long: I ward off, defend myself against, resist, defend, assist.
ἀμύνομαι.sd: to ward off (for oneself), i.e. protect
ἀμύνομαι.der: middle voice of a primary verb;
ἀμύνομαι.as:
ἀμύνω,
[in LXX (mid.): Jos 10:13 (נקם), נָקַם), Ps 118:10-12מוּל hi.), Is 59:16 (ישׁע hi.), Wi 11:3, al.;]
to ward off, etc. Mid.
(a)to defend oneself against;
(b)to requite;
(c) = act., to defend, assist (Is 59:16): c. acc. pers., Ac 7:24 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀμάρτυρος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a form of G3144 (μάρτυς);

Ἀμφίπολις.long: Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia.
Ἀμφίπολις.sd: a city surrounded by a river; Amphipolis, a place in Macedonia
Ἀμφίπολις.der: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G4172 (πόλις);
Ἀμφίπολις.as:
Ἀμφίπολις, -εως, ἡ
Amphipolis, in Macedonia, so called because the river Strymon flowed around it: Ac 17:1.†

ἀμετανόητος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3340 (μετανοέω);
ἀμετανόητος.as:
*† ἀμετανόητος, -ον
(< μετανοέω),
1.impenitent: Ro 2:5
2. = ἀμεταμέλητος (π., Philo, al.; v. Deiss., BS, 257; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀμεταμέλητος.long: not to be repented of, about which no change of mind can take place, not affected by change of mind.
ἀμεταμέλητος.kj: without repentance, not to be repented of
ἀμεταμέλητος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3338 (μεταμέλλομαι);
ἀμεταμέλητος.as:
* ἀ-μεταμέλητος, -ον
(< μεταμέλομαι),
not repented of, unregretted: Ro 11:29, II Co 7:10.†

Ἀμπλιᾶτος.long: Ampliatus (Amplias), a male member of the church at Rome, probably of the imperial household.
Ἀμπλιᾶτος.as:
Ἀμπλιᾶτος (T, -ίατος; Rec. Ἀμπλιᾶς; v. MM, VGT, 5.v.), -ου, ὁ,
Ampliatus: Ro 16:8.†

ἀμετακίνητος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3334 (μετακινέω);

ἄμετρος.long: not measurable, immeasurable, to a limitless degree.
ἄμετρος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3358 (μέτρον);
ἄμετρος.as:
* ἄμετρος, -ον
(< μέτρον),
without measure: adverbially, εἰς τὰ ἄ., excessively, II Co 10:1310:15†

ἄμωμος.kj: without blame (blemish, fault, spot), faultless, unblamable
ἄμωμος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3470 (μῶμος);
ἄμωμος.as:
ἄ-μωμος, -ον
(< μῶμος, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for תָּמִים];
of sacrificial victims, without blemish: of Christ, He 9:14, I Pe 1:19; ethically, unblemished, faultless: Eph 1:45:27, Phl 2:15, Col 1:22, Ju 24, Re 14:5 (Cremer, 425, 788; MM, VGT, s.v.).†
SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄσπιλος.

ἀμέμπτως.as:
ἀ-μέμπτως,
adv.
(< ἄμεμπτος), [in LXX: Es 3:13*;]
blamelessly (Lft., Notes, 28, 89; MM, VGT, s.v. -ος): I Th 2:103:13 WH mg., 5:23.†

ἄμαχος.long: peaceable, abstaining from fighting, not contentious.
ἄμαχος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3163 (μάχη);
ἄμαχος.as:
* ἄμαχος, -ον
(< μάχη);
1.invincible (freq. in cl.).
2.abstaining from fighting, non-combatant (Xen.). Metaph. (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), not contentious: I Ti 3:3, Tit 3:2.†

ἀμοιβή.long: a change, an exchange; hence plur: reciprocal good deeds (services), a fitting requital.
ἀμοιβή.as:
** ἀμοιβή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἀμείβομαι, to repay); [in Aq., Sm.: Pr 12:14, al.;]
requital, recompense: I Ti 5:4 (for illustration from π. v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀμετάθετος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3346 (μετατίθημι);
ἀμετάθετος.as:
*† ἀ-μετάθετος, -ον
(< μετατίθημι), [in LXX: III Mac 5:1,12*;]
immutable: He 6:18; as subst., τὸ ἀ., immutability, He 6:17 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀμήτωρ.g: whose mother's name is not recorded or known
ἀμήτωρ.long: (lit: motherless), whose mother's name is not recorded (or known).
ἀμήτωρ.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3384 (μήτηρ);
ἀμήτωρ.as:
* ἀμήτωρ, -ορος, ὁ, ἡ
(< μήτηρ),
without a mother (freq. in Gk. writers of the gods): ἀπάτωρ ἀ. of one without recorded genealogy, He 7:3 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).

ἀμίαντος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3392 (μιαίνω);
ἀμίαντος.as:
** ἀ-μίαντος, -ον
(< μιαίνω), [in LXX: Wi 3:134:28:20, II Mac 14:3615:34*;]
undefiled, free from contamination (in π., of αἰθήρ; MM, VGT, s.v.): He 7:2613:4, I Pe 1:4, Ja 1:27.†
SYN.: ἄμωμος, ἄσπιλος (Cremer, 784).

ἀμάω.sd: properly, to collect, i.e. (by implication) reap
ἀμάω.as:
* ἀμάω, -ῶ
(in cl. chiefly poët.),
to reap: Ja 5:4.†

ἀμάραντος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3133 (μαραίνω);
ἀμάραντος.as:
**† ἀμάραντος, -ον
(< μαραίνομαι), [in LXX: Wi 6:12 (σοφία)*;]
unfading (whence ὁ ἀ., the amaranth, an unfading flower): I Pe 1:4 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀμαράντινος.as:
*† ἀμαράντινος, -ον
(< ἀμάραντος),
of amaranth (Inscr.); hence unfading: I Pe 5:4.†

ἀμώμητος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3469 (μωμάομαι);
ἀμώμητος.as:
* ἀ-μώμητος, -ου
(< μωμάομαι),
blameless: II Pe 3:14.†
SYN.: ἄμεμπτος (q.v.), ἀνέγκλητος, ἀνεπίλημπτος.

ἀμαθής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3129 (μανθάνω);
ἀμαθής.as:
** ἀμαθής, -ές
(< μανθάνω), [in Sm.: Ps 49:11*;]
unlearned, ignorant: II Pe 3:16 (on the rareness of this word, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἄμωμον.as:
* ἄμωμον, -ου, τό,
amomum, a fragrant plant of India (RV, spice): Re 18:13.

ἀμέθυστος.long: amethyst (a kind of rock crystal: the best specimens are the color of unmixed wine, whence perhaps the name), believed to stave off drunkenness.
ἀμέθυστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3184 (μεθύω);
ἀμέθυστος.as:
ἀμέθυστος, -ου, ἡ
(acc. to Plut., < ἀ-μεθύω, being regarded as an antidote against drunkenness), [in LXX: Ex 28:1936:1939:12Ez 28:13*;]
amethyst, a purple quartz: Re 21:20.†
